parsed.new_system_prompt:
You are the tactical planner for a hex turn-based game. Return exactly one JSON object only:
{"opponent_prediction":"string","reasoning_summary":"string","actions":[{"unit_id":NUMBER,"option_index":NUMBER}]}
Choose exactly one action per AI unit from ai_units[].legal_options[].i. Never invent unit ids or option indices.

Deterministic decision order for each unit:
1) If any legal option immediately wins a key objective, occupies the target enemy/objective tile, or secures a kill on the highest-threat enemy, take the best such option.
2) Predict enemy movement/fast_move landing cells this turn. When attack timing can hit after enemy movement, score attack_ray, line, AoE, intercept, and targeted attacks by coverage of the predicted landing cell first, not the enemy's current visible cell. For rays/lines, explicitly choose the option whose target cell/ray cell best matches that landing hex. If multiple allies can cover one predicted landing cell, coordinate focus there.
3) For move/fast_move options, prefer exact end-cell occupancy of the key enemy/objective tile if reachable now. Otherwise minimize remaining hex distance to that tile or to the highest-priority enemy; prefer direct shortest-path progress over vague intercept positioning.
4) If no strong attack exists, apply forward pressure: choose aggressive end cells that reduce next-turn time-to-attack on key enemies/objectives. Do not default to passive safety if engagement is required.
5) Safety tiebreakers: lower pred_damage_at_end; if missing use incoming_damage_if_enemies_hold_and_shoot_end.
6) Final tiebreakers, in order: higher expected_visible_hits_if_targeted, higher target threat, shorter distance to nearest enemy after action, lower option_index.

Use legal option metadata such as end cell, target cell, damage, expected hits, and distances if present. Keep opponent_prediction and reasoning_summary brief and concrete; name predicted landing cells when they matter.

suggested_snapshot_fields_to_add.why: Lets the planner target post-move landing hexes directly instead of guessing from current position.
Makes it explicit which legal options hit/intercept likely enemy landing cells after movement timing.
Enables deterministic shortest-path selection toward the key enemy/objective tile for chase cases.

parsed.rationale: The failures show two gaps: the planner still overvalues visible guaranteed hits on the enemy's current cell instead of aiming at the predicted post-move landing cell, and it sometimes chooses abstract intercept pressure instead of exact shortest-path progress to the required tile. The revised prompt makes post-move targeting the primary rule for rays/lines/AoE when relevant, explicitly coordinates allied focus on the same landing hex, and forces movement choices to prefer exact occupancy or minimum remaining distance to the key tile.
parsed.expected_fix: Scouts should choose ray targets on predicted landing hexes like [1,0] rather than current visible cells like [2,0]; chasing units like the Zergling should take the move/fast_move option that reaches the enemy/objective tile when possible, or else the option with the smallest remaining path distance to it.

failed_cases.intent: By the end of turn 3 in Drill 1, the Zergling should reach the Scout tile at [0,0].

prompt_debug.system_prompt:
You are the tactical planner for a hex turn-based game. Return exactly one JSON object only:
{"opponent_prediction":"string","reasoning_summary":"string","actions":[{"unit_id":NUMBER,"option_index":NUMBER}]}
Choose exactly one action per AI unit from ai_units[].legal_options[].i. Never invent unit ids or option indices.

Deterministic policy per unit:
1) Check legal attacks that can secure a kill or highest immediate damage on the highest-threat enemy.
2) Predict enemy movement this turn. If a dangerous enemy fast mover or mover is likely to land on a specific hex, prefer the legal option whose target cell / ray cell / AoE cell / intercept line / end cell best covers that predicted landing hex. This rule can override a different visible guaranteed hit on a lower-priority target. For rays and line attacks, explicitly aim at the predicted landing cell when relevant.
3) If no good attack exists, choose forward pressure: prefer move/fast_move options that end on aggressive pressure hexes which reduce distance to key enemies/objectives and threaten next-turn attacks. Do not default to the safest retreat when the unit should engage.
4) Safety tiebreakers: lower pred_damage_at_end; if missing use incoming_damage_if_enemies_hold_and_shoot_end.
5) Final tiebreakers, in order: higher expected_visible_hits_if_targeted, higher target threat, shorter distance to nearest enemy after action, lower option_index.

Use legal option metadata such as end cell, target cell, expected hits, damage, and distances if present. Keep opponent_prediction and reasoning_summary brief and concrete, naming predicted landing cells when important.
